reconcile.note: Gill limits 1 Timothy's command to pray for all men to people of every rank, not every individual, exempting those who like Judah have sinned past intercession.

discrepancy.emptyNote: Steve Wells catalogues this as a contradiction, but the project's public-domain source survey found no verbatim critic passage that engages it.
discrepancy.emptyNoteAttr: Steve Wells, The Skeptic's Annotated Bible, "Should you pray for everyone?" (skepticsannotatedbible.com/contra/pray_for_everyone.html) (2013).

sides.snippet: don't you pray for this people, neither lift up a cry nor prayer for them
sides.verseText: Therefore don't you pray for this people, neither lift up a cry nor prayer for them, neither make intercession to me; for I will not hear you.

sides.snippet: petitions, prayers, intercessions, and givings of thanks, be made for all men
sides.verseText: I exhort therefore, first of all, that petitions, prayers, intercessions, and givings of thanks, be made for all men:
